text.p: - According to the final unofficial results of Sunday's general election, the Liberal Democrats will get 25 seats, the People's Party 19, Social Democrats 16, Christian Democrats 10 and the United List nine seats in the 90 seat parliament.
- Electricity distribution company Eles has threatened to hike electricity prices by 13.4 percent on Saturday, unless the government itself raises prices by Thursday.
- Four Netherland's Air-force F-16 fighter planes will participate in a Slovenian military exercise on Thursday.
- Slovenian Prime Minister Davorin Kracun met ambassadors of the European Union and NATO member states in Slovenia on Wednesday to discuss Slovenia's current integration efforts.

- Slovenia's DeSUS party, largely backed by pensioners, said it would support the reelection of current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek. Unofficial final results give the party five seats in the 90 seat legislature.
- Slovenia's airforce needs 10 to 15 fighter aircraft, deputy chief of staff of Slovenian army, Iztok Podbregar said.
- The national radio and television board will elect a general manager from six candidates on Thursday.

- A survey by daily Dnevnik showed that 53.6 percent of voters think Janez Drnovsek should remain the Prime Minster, 15.1 percent supported Marjan Podobnik and seven percent Janez Jansa, while 22.3 percent were undecided.
- Pharmaceuticals producer Krka is expected to complete its privatisation soon, the company's representatives said on Wednesday.
